articles.title: 讯飞星火 X2.6 端云一体大模型发布，首次基于全国产算力实现代码和智能体能力突破
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，在今日下午的科大讯飞全球 1024 开发者节活动中，讯飞星火 X2.6 端云一体大模型正式发布。讯飞星火 X2.6 宣称首次基于全国产算力实现代码和智能体能力突破。科大讯飞董事长刘庆峰表示，只有星火一家是用全国产算力训练的，其他全是在 N 卡上训练，而且科大讯飞的尺寸是最小的。此外，刘庆峰表示讯飞星火 X2.6 率先突破国产芯片长程任务的训练效率瓶颈，适配国产平台的长程任务动态并行训练技术，解决了因为国产芯片显存带宽限制导致的混合训练效率低下问题。对于国产算力集群在长程任务上的推理效率，科大讯飞也实现了两个重要创新：一个是基于国产异构算力的分布式推理技术，解决国产芯片显存带宽限制导致的训不快问题。另一个是提出基于国产设备的开发技术，很多东西都不用重新再计算，直接用原有结果就可以。此外，星火 X2.6-4B 开源端侧大模型正式发布，率先实现端侧大模型智能体能力阶跃，相比 X2.5-4B 模型的各项跑分都有明显提升。IT之家从发布会获悉，9 月 1 日星火 X2.5-4B 端侧模型开源以来，下载量已进入全球端侧模型前四。讯飞星火 X2.6 系列模型现已在讯飞星火官网开放试用，首发星火大模型端云一体协同架构。讯飞星火 X2.6 基于国产算力完成训练，采用 293B-A30B 参数的 MoE 架构，上下文长度拓展至 1M，代码与智能体能力达业界一流水平，同时提供专业安全防护并支持按任务场景自定义安全策略，推理定价为：输入限时 0.9 元 / 百万 tokens输入缓存命中限时 0.08 元 / 百万 tokens输出限时 3.6 元 / 百万 tokens讯飞星火 X2.6-4B 开源端侧大模型在代码、智能体、长文本及多语言能力上实现大幅提升，新增三档推理模式，自研推理框架下的推理效率较 ollama 有所提升，推理定价限时免费。

articles.title: Win10/Win11 学院：如何靠“任务计划程序”错峰启动应用，缓解开机卡顿
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，科技媒体 NeoWin 昨日（10 月 21 日）发布博文，介绍了在 Windows 11 系统中，如何借助系统自带的“任务计划程序”，错峰启动应用，从而缓解开机卡顿。该媒体指出，不少 Windows 用户习惯让聊天、云盘、游戏启动器等应用随系统自动运行，但当启动项过多后，登录后的头一两分钟常会明显卡顿，在配置较低的电脑上表现尤为明显。在 Windows 10、Windows 11 系统中，微软官方并未提供“延迟启动”选项，但用户可以按照以下步骤，让重要程序立即打开，而非必要程序延后运行，从而分散系统资源占用。IT之家援引博文介绍，附上让 Windows 11 稍后启动应用的步骤如下：1、前往“设置”>“应用”>“启动”，禁用您想要延迟启动的应用。这一点很重要，否则 Windows 可能会正常启动该应用，然后任务计划程序稍后又会再次启动它。2、按 Win + R，输入 taskschd.msc，然后按回车键打开任务计划程序。3、在右侧窗格中，单击“创建任务”。给任务起一个名称，用于表明它属于哪个应用程序。4、打开“触发器”选项卡，然后单击“新建”。将“开始任务”设置为“登录时”。5、启用“延迟任务时间”功能，并选择 Windows 在启动应用程序之前等待的时间并点击确定。对于非必要程序，通常等待一到两分钟就足够了，以便 Windows 先完成桌面和后台服务的加载。小编这里使用的是 Windows 10 系统，Windows 11 系统操作步骤相同。6、接下来切换到“操作”选项卡，点击“新建”7、将操作设置为“启动程序”，然后浏览到应用程序的可执行文件并选择它。如果您不确定可执行文件的位置，通常可以从应用程序的快捷方式属性或安装文件夹中找到它。8、单击“确定”保存任务。

articles.title: eBay 回应中国区裁员 80% 传闻：系臆测，未退出中国市场
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，近日有传闻称，eBay 中国于本周启动新一轮人员调整，涉及上海等主要办公点，中国区裁员比例或已达 80%。据蓝鲸新闻消息，eBay 相关负责人对此回应称，公司昨日进行了全球人员调整，中国是其中一部分；80% 的说法是臆测，CEO 表示此次调整影响了全球 9% 的员工。该负责人还表示，网上有很多相关消息，但可以肯定的是，eBay 并未关闭中国研发中心，也未退出中国市场；我们面向卖家的活动仍在稳步推进，12 月还将举办年度汽配卖家盛会。据IT之家此前援引法新社消息，美国电子商务平台 eBay 于当地时间 10 月 21 日表示，将裁员约 1000 个岗位。这大约占其总员工的 9%。该公司表示，这一决定“是为了确保我们保持强势地位”。为此，eBay 希望“使其劳动力和资源与战略优先事项保持一致”。

articles.title: 软银股价较 6 月高点接近腰斩，AI 投资烧钱模式遭市场质疑
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，据彭博社报道，随着融资成本不断上升，投资者开始质疑软银集团能否持续投入巨额资金发展人工智能，软银市值可能较 6 月高点腰斩。当地时间 22 日，软银股价盘中一度下跌 6.7%，较 6 月 2 日创下的历史最高点累计跌幅达到 50%。美国超大市值企业的财报表现，也未能打消市场疑虑。市场对 AI 投资的担忧此前因美国云计算服务商 CoreWeave 陷入债务困境而加剧。CoreWeave 的债券价格跌至困境债券水平，暴露出整个行业面临的融资风险。Nagomi Capital 投资管理主管村松一之指出，投资者越来越关注 AI 企业的财务健康状况。软银高度依赖借贷融资，加上融资成本不断上升，使其财务风险显得尤为突出。如果全球市场对 AI 增长前景转为悲观，软银愿景基金的投资资产可能贬值，进而推高集团今后的融资风险溢价。软银的信用风险也在上升。当地时间 20 日，用于对冲软银债务违约风险的信用违约互换报价升至近四年高点。软银在 AI 领域的投资遍及基础设施、能源和机器人等产业，其中大部分依靠举债筹资。CoreWeave 的债务问题不仅引发债券投资者担忧，也动摇了此前看重软银 AI 投资回报的股票投资者信心。软银股价本月累计下跌超过 30%，9 月的涨幅全部回吐。AI 模型市场竞争加剧也持续给软银带来压力。软银向 OpenAI 投资了近 650 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4,348.06 亿元人民币），但 OpenAI 面临越来越多来自中国的竞争对手，后者能够以更低的价格提供性能相近的模型。今年 9 月，软银发行了 111 亿美元（现汇率约合 742.52 亿元人民币）的垃圾债券，创下企业垃圾债发行规模的历史纪录，以支持创始人孙正义雄心勃勃的 AI 投资计划。

articles.title: 工信部 NVDB 发布关于防范 PHP 远程代码执行超危漏洞的风险提示
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，近日，工业和信息化部网络安全威胁和漏洞信息共享平台（NVDB）监测发现，PHP 存在两个远程代码执行超危漏洞，危害严重。PHP 是一款广泛用于 Web 开发的开源服务器端脚本语言。由于其存在两个超危远程代码执行漏洞，未经身份验证的攻击者可利用其远程执行任意代码，造成服务器受控、敏感信息泄露、业务中断等危害。受影响的 PHP 范围包括：8.5 系列＜8.5.12、8.4 系列＜8.4.27、8.3 系列＜8.3.36、8.2 系列＜8.2.35、8.1 系列及更早版本。目前，PHP 安全团队已修复漏洞并发布安全公告（URL 链接：https://www.php.net/ archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5）。建议相关单位和用户立即开展全面排查，及时升级至最新安全版本，或采取临时下线、关闭会话上传进度功能、网络隔离、网络访问限制等临时防护措施；加强网络安全监测和管理，及时修改账号、口令和密钥等凭证，防范网络攻击风险。相关阅读：《影响约 70% 网站：PHP 高危漏洞被修复，OpenAI 牵头协调全球发现 / 修复》《为预防 PHP 安全漏洞，芬兰政府临时关闭部分网站》《PHP 将推补丁修复两个 9.2 分漏洞，欧盟敦促无法及时修复的机构下线受影响网站》《9.2 评分：PHP 拉响安全警报，今天将修复 2 个高危漏洞》

articles.title: 消息称索尼 PS6 物料成本比微软 XBOX Helix 游戏主机低约 200 美元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，消息源 @Kepler_L2 昨日（10 月 21 日）在 X 平台发布推文，称索尼下一代主机 PS6 的整机物料清单（BOM）成本，将比微软下一代游戏主机 Project Helix 方案低约 200 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,338 元人民币）。科技媒体 gamingbolt 指出，微软下一代 XBOX 主机将采用代号为 Magnus 的核心芯片，由 AMD 联合设计开发，规模更大，性能也预计略强于 PS6 芯片：PS6 芯片算力约为 40 TFLOPS，Magnus 则约为 56 TFLOPS。IT之家此前援引 KeplerL2 爆料，索尼 PlayStation 6 主机仅内存与 NAND 闪存两项物料成本就超过 680 美元（现汇率约合 4,549 元人民币），因此最终零售价格可能会超过 1,000 美元（现汇率约合 6,689 元人民币）。不过该消息源解释称，主机研发通常需要五年以上，索尼和微软最初并不打算让新主机售价超过 1,000 美元（现汇率约合 6,689 元人民币）；但内存与 NAND 闪存价格大幅上涨，令成本压力远超预期。尽管有声音建议两家公司推迟发布、等待存储价格回落，但爆料称 PS6 与 Project Helix 的芯片均已完成流片，生产流程已难以推迟。按当前传闻，次世代主机可能于 2027 年底至 2028 年初登场。相关阅读：《消息称索尼 PS6 仅内存和存储物料成本就超 680 美元》

articles.title: 欧洲 9 月新车销量同比增长 10%，中国品牌抢占大部分增量市场
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，欧洲汽车销量上月增速加快，延续今年以来的上涨态势，消费者持续转向电动汽车，而新增销量当中很大一部分由中国车企拿下。欧洲汽车制造商协会当地时间周四公布，9 月新车注册量同比上涨 10%，达到 136 万辆，实现连续第八个月增长。纯电动汽车与插电混动车型合计占总销量的 43%，去年这一比例为 32%；法国与德国的电池汽车销量近乎翻倍。中东战争推高燃油价格，让电动汽车的经济性优势进一步凸显，同时法国、德国的补贴政策也有助于降低电动汽车较高的售价。但这场能源冲击也可能压缩家庭预算、打击消费信心，抑制大额商品消费需求。向好的市场给大众集团等欧洲车企带来了一丝喘息空间。这些企业正承受多重压力：中国市场需求疲软、贸易壁垒，以及本土的降本压力。不过向电动汽车转型这件事，利弊兼具。大众、斯泰兰蒂斯、宝马等车企，电动汽车的利润依旧低于同级别燃油车，意味着转型需要付出代价。与此同时，比亚迪、奇瑞正在欧洲本土市场不断加剧竞争。彭博行业研究数据显示，今年至今中国品牌的注册量已经翻番有余，机构预计欧洲市场的增量大部分会被中国品牌获取。奇瑞热销的 Jaecoo 7 就是爆款车型之一，不少消费者在这款中国 SUV 和大众旗下斯柯达 Elroq 之间做选择。IT之家注意到，9 月特斯拉销量持续回暖，交付量大涨 73%。在中国车企里，奇瑞增幅领跑，销量近乎翻两番，在欧洲的市场份额几乎翻倍，达到 3.9%。行业裁员潮愈演愈烈，处境艰难的欧洲老牌车企获得了更多政策层面支持。本月早些时候，欧盟与中国原则上达成协议，对涌入欧洲的中国混动汽车设置进口上限。法国与德国也达成共识，两国将共同游说欧盟，进一步放宽 2035 年新车燃油车碳排放严苛限值。两国统一立场，也有望推动“欧洲本土制造”相关法规落地，以此扶持本土制造业。

articles.title: 知情人士：马斯克公开支持 SpaceX、特斯拉合并，恐给谈判添乱
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，今天（22 日）午间，据路透社援引直接参与了解谈判的知情人士消息称，马斯克公开支持旗下 SpaceX 与特斯拉进行一项价值 3.5 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 23.41 万亿元人民币）的合并交易，引发了部分参与谈判的内部人士担忧。他们认为，马斯克的表态可能招致股东质疑，使交易进程推迟数周。该人士称，马斯克公开谈论合并计划给谈判添了乱，外界可能因此质疑特斯拉股东的利益能否得到充分保障。部分参与者联想到特斯拉 2016 年收购 SolarCity 的交易。当年，马斯克在收购过程中发挥的作用引发争议，双方为此打了多年官司。马斯克同时担任 SpaceX 和特斯拉的 CEO，并持有两家公司的大量股份。本周，他向投资者证实，双方正研究一项可能创下企业交易规模纪录的合并计划，并各自成立了特别委员会负责评估。马斯克的表态引发内部反对的情况，此前未见报道。三名知情人士透露，双方均聘请了顾问，但谈判仍处于初期阶段。其中一人称，SpaceX 最近几周主动接洽特斯拉，双方讨论了多种合并方案，包括由 SpaceX 直接收购特斯拉，或成立一家新的控股公司，将两家公司合并至其旗下。双方还在研究如何支付交易对价，包括完全以股票进行交易。上述谈判细节此前也未被披露。对于 SpaceX 与特斯拉这样的关联交易，通常需要由独立董事负责监督，以保障公众股东的利益。特斯拉 2016 年收购 SolarCity 时，独立董事能否保障股东利益便成为争议焦点。股东当时指控，马斯克干预收购程序，试图挽救自己对 SolarCity 的投资，由此引发持续多年的诉讼。SolarCity 由马斯克的表亲创立，主要从事屋顶太阳能业务，当时经营状况不佳。马斯克在交易发生时，分别持有特斯拉和 SolarCity 约 22% 的股份。股东认为，马斯克直接参与并公开支持收购，损害了交易的公平性。争议的核心之一，是马斯克对特斯拉的实际控制权。股东主张，虽然马斯克并非多数股东，但凭借与董事会成员的密切关系，以及强势的行事风格，他实际上拥有控股股东的影响力。特拉华州最高法院后来指出，原告提出的交易缺乏独立委员会，以及马斯克参与和公开支持收购的其他若干事实，足以支持交易程序不公平的认定。不过，法院最终仍认定收购本身公平。案件经过数年才告解决，特斯拉董事还支付了 6,000 万美元（现汇率约合 4.01 亿元人民币），以和解针对他们的指控。马斯克持有特斯拉近 20% 的股份，以及 SpaceX 略低于 50% 的股份。分析师认为，合并或让他取得新公司的控制权。马斯克在周二的投资者电话会议上承认，由于自身存在利益冲突，他不能参与特别委员会的讨论。知情人士称，交易顾问还与马斯克的律师保持沟通，确保他不介入合并谈判。上述知情人士称，参与合并谈判的人员担心，马斯克公开支持合并并披露谈判消息，会引发投资者更严格的审视。在独立董事评估交易期间，存在利益冲突的当事方通常会避免公开表态。一旦特斯拉与 SpaceX 完成合并，不仅将创下全球企业交易规模纪录，还会诞生全球最大的工业与科技集团之一。交易规模将超过今年早些时候 SpaceX 收购 xAI 的交易，后者也是有史以来宣布的最大企业交易之一。

articles.title: 谷歌 Google Cloud 计划部署至多 96 万块 GPU 的英伟达 Vera Rubin 平台
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，Google（谷歌）云服务业务 Google Cloud 当地时间 21 日宣布，其计划将基于 NVIDIA（英伟达）Vera Rubin 平台的基础设施扩展到多个算力站点，最多可部署 96 万个 Rubin GPU。Google Cloud 同日表示，其基于 NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 机架级系统的 A5X 实例正式上线。该实例采用了 NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNIC 以及 Google Cloud 的 Virgo 网络和第四代先进液冷技术，将于下个月正式推出。其它方面，Google Cloud 将成为首批在裸机实例上提供机架级 NVIDIA 机密计算服务的云服务提供商之一。此外，谷歌云还将在搭载 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 服务器版本 GPU 的 G4 虚拟机上正式推出机密计算服务。

articles.title: 5 年内产量翻番：马斯克称特斯拉目标 2030 实现年产量破 500 万辆
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，科技媒体 breakingthenews 今天（10 月 22 日）发布博文，报道称在最新财报电话会议上，特斯拉首席执行官埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）表示，公司有望在 2030 年实现年产量突破 500 万辆。马斯克表示特斯拉“已经为更大规模制造能力打下基础”，并认为“有很好的机会实现这一目标”。IT之家援引博文介绍，根据特斯拉第三季度财报资料，公司目前年产能约为 240 万辆；若 2030 年达到 500 万辆，相当于产能翻倍。马斯克强调，当前特斯拉车辆需求“正在快速增长”，并且“明显超过产能”。公司正在通过提升现有工厂生产节奏、扩建柏林工厂、在得州推进 Cybercab 量产，以及启动新的 Semi 工厂等方式增加产能。财报电话会还披露，特斯拉第三季度交付 486,532 辆汽车，管理层称交付主要受产能而非需求限制，未交付订单积压达到近四年高位。马斯克将需求增长部分归因于完全自动驾驶（FSD）软件，并称公司将继续推动 FSD 在欧洲等更多市场获得批准。

articles.title: 总台菁彩声车载测试序列发布，可在车上感受沉浸式三维环绕音效
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，据央视新闻报道，以“菁彩无界 智启全球”为主题的 2026 UWA SUMMIT（世界超高清视频产业联盟产业发展大会）于 10 月 21 日在广东深圳举行。大会旨在聚合超高清全产业链资源，深化跨行业协同合作，加速超高清视音频技术创新与商业化落地，构建具备国际竞争力的产业生态。聚焦 AI 赋能超高清视音频产业，大会集中发布标准、技术等成果超 20 项。其中，中央广播电视总台国家重点实验室项目菁彩声车载测试序列正式发布，并登陆总台云听客户端。作为专门面向汽车座舱环境打造的 Audio Vivid 标准音频序列，该套素材分为功能测试、欣赏体验两大组别，覆盖声道校准、声像定位、人声、器乐、交响乐、流行音乐、环境音效等多类内容，既可供车企、研发人员对车载菁彩声系统开展标准化测试，也面向广大车主提供沉浸式音源，打开云听，就能在车上感受沉浸式三维环绕音效。该技术补齐了菁彩声车载场景标准内容短板，助力行业统一评测标尺，加速菁彩声在智能网联汽车产业的规模化应用落地。IT之家从报道获悉，世界超高清视频产业联盟自 2022 年 1 月成立以来，累计发布标准 100 项，其中国家标准 6 项，国际标准 6 项，包括菁彩视听制作、传输和应用。联盟会员单位已超过 500 家，覆盖 30 个国家和地区，其中海外企业 69 家。采用菁彩视听技术的产品覆盖面越来越广，家庭场景机顶盒发货超 3500 万台，车载场景装车量突破 350 万台；主流平台上线超 30 万小时菁彩视听内容、800 万首菁彩声歌曲和乐曲、1000 余部有声剧。下一步，联盟要持续推进 ITU、IEC、DVB、SMPTE 等国际组织和内容制播机构、设备企业的合作，支持联盟会员走向国际市场，让菁彩视听技术惠及世界。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，CORSAIR（海盗船）当地时间昨日正式推出了 1200W 版本的 2026 款 RMe 电源。该型号率先配备支持 PinProtect 逐供电针脚过流保护的 12V-2×6 接口，可保护显卡免受意外电源波动的冲击。RM1200e (2026) 长 150mm，采用全模组线材设计，配套压纹线缆套件。其采用工业级 105℃ 日本电解电容和半桥 LLC 拓扑，符合 ATX12V 3.1、PCIe CEM 5.1 规范，获得 Cybenetics 铂金转换效率认证。该电源拥有三维 Y 形风扇格栅，内置 140mm 大直径风扇，支持 ZERO RPM 模式，获得 Cybenetics LAMDA A 噪声等级认证。其拥有完善的八项安全防护机制，持续工作温度达 50℃，享受 10 年质保。IT之家了解到，海盗船 2026 款 RM1200e 电源可选黑 / 白 2 种配色，售价 204.99 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,371 元人民币）。

articles.title: 消息称《鬼灭之刃：无限城篇第二章》动画电影 2027 年 9 月上映
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，Polygon 昨日（10 月 21 日）发布博文，报道称《鬼灭之刃：无限城篇第二章》动画电影可能会在 2027 年 9 月 15 日发行上映。电影信息网站 The-Numbers.com 近期收录了一部未命名动画电影，由索尼影业与 Crunchyroll 联合发行，定档于 2027 年 9 月 15 日。IT之家附上相关截图如下：由于索尼及 Crunchyroll 持有《鬼灭之刃》系列的全球发行与流媒体权利，且索尼旗下 Aniplex 也参与该系列制作委员会，不少粉丝推测该神秘电影就是《鬼灭之刃：无限城篇第二章》。另一个候选者是已宣布将于 2027 年夏季上映的《海贼王剧场版：神之谷》。但该系列由东映动画制作，而上述未命名影片的资料并未提及东映；索尼 / Crunchyroll 虽负责《海贼王》电影在北美的发行，却不负责列表中提到的法国市场发行。《鬼灭之刃剧场版：无限城第一章》作为三部曲首部，全球票房已达 7.93 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 53.05 亿元人民币），成为影史票房最高的动画电影之一，因此续集的上映时间自然备受关注。相关阅读：《〈鬼灭之刃：无限城篇第一章〉剧场版动画电影 7 月 28 日上线流媒体，登陆 Crunchyroll 与 Netflix》《“鬼灭”首登内地大银幕，动画电影〈鬼灭之刃：无限城篇第一章猗窝座再袭〉国内定档 11 月 14 日》《卷均 956 万册历史第二：人气漫画〈鬼灭之刃〉全球累计发行量破 2 亿》

articles.title: 特斯拉 App 适配苹果首款折叠 iPhone Duo，引入大屏双栏体验
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，科技媒体 notateslaapp 今天（10 月 22 日）发布博文，报道称特斯拉面向 iPad、iPhone Duo，推送 4.62.0 版本更新，重点针对大屏幕和折叠手机重新设计界面。IT之家附上相关演示视频如下：报道指出 iPad 用户此前只能使用被拉伸放大的 iPhone 版应用，而新版则采用专属大屏布局，左侧为功能菜单，右侧呈现更精细的车辆可视化界面，可同时查看更多车辆信息。针对苹果折叠屏 iPhone Duo，应用在内屏采用大屏布局，可同时展示充电信息、实时摄像头和行车记录仪片段；合上手机后，外屏自动切换回常规手机界面。新界面保留了手机版的核心功能，包括车辆控制、空调、位置、自动驾驶、召唤、充电、日程设置、安全与驾驶员管理以及安全评分等。用户打开“充电”等功能后，子菜单仍保留在左侧，详情内容则占据屏幕其余区域，操作层级更清晰。新版还更新车辆可视化部分，更接近车内停车界面的效果，背景颜色会匹配车漆，地面还带有反射效果。用户可直接通过该界面开关前备箱、后备箱，锁止或解锁车辆，并查看充电状态。特斯拉还新增了“自定义控制”入口，方便用户调整闪光、鸣笛、启动、通风等快捷按钮；新增的“显示 PSI”按钮则可将胎压直接显示在车辆可视化界面上，减少进入深层菜单的操作。

articles.title: 三星心系天下新品发布会定档 10 月 29 日，W27 系列折叠屏手机将至
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，三星官方今日宣布，三星心系天下新品发布会定档 10 月 29 日 16:00，海报中出现了两款折叠屏手机的剪影。据IT之家此前报道，有三星授权体验店发布预告，心系天下 W27 新品发布会将于 10 月 29 日举行。消息显示，新机预计将于 11 月 5 日开启首批门店取机，高端旗舰折叠现开启优先预定。按照以往惯例，三星 W27 心系天下手机预计基于 Galaxy Z Fold8 系列手机打造。三星 Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra 手机于今年 7 月发布，起售价 14999 元。作为参考，Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra 配备一块 6.5 英寸 FHD+ 外屏，覆盖 Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 玻璃。内屏为 8 英寸 QXGA+ 折叠屏，支持抗反射涂层，峰值亮度最高可达 3000 尼特。▲ Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra影像系统方面，Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra 后置三摄，包括一颗 2 亿像素广角主摄（F1.7 光圈、支持 2 倍光学变焦）、一颗 5000 万像素超广角镜头（F2.2 光圈），以及一颗 1000 万像素长焦镜头（F2.4 光圈、支持 3 倍光学变焦）。内外屏分别配备一颗 1000 万像素前置摄像头。性能方面，Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra 搭载基于 3nm 工艺打造的第五代骁龙 8 至尊版（for Galaxy）处理器。存储组合包括 12GB+256GB、12GB+512GB 以及 16GB+1TB 三个版本。续航方面，新机采用硅碳（Silicon-Carbon）电池，容量达到 5000mAh，支持 45W 有线快充和 20W 无线充电。

Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. Using corporate financial reports as its data source, Navalia semantically selects supporting evidence from complete fact sets and constructs executable computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable evidence and actual data dependencies between steps. articles.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26904v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent studies have proposed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) methods that enable LLMs to generate high-quality RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Existing approaches optimize circuit PPA (Power, Performance, Area) by aggregating multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, making it difficult to simultaneously generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions across different trade-offs such as low power, low latency, and small area. However, in practical design, the relative importance of each objective varies depending on product requirements and design constraints; thus, obtaining a diverse and high-quality candidate set is beneficial in that designers can choose a preferred trade-off a posteriori. articles.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26913v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. articles.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26924v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verifying analytical results both during evolution and after task assembly. articles.content:

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are enabling agents to move beyond predefined workflows toward autonomous planning and execution, creating new opportunities for smart manufacturing. However, dynamic environments, complex physical constraints, and stringent reliability requirements hinder the direct deployment of general-purpose agents in smart manufacturing. This article presents a systematic overview of LLM-driven industrial agents. First, we analyze five key challenges and discuss the concept and core characteristics of industrial agents. We then establish a unified taxonomy covering application scenarios, embodiment forms, and five capability levels. Next, we propose a four-layer system architecture and detail its core modules and operational mechanisms for closed-loop task execution. articles.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark. Abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. articles.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conversational recommender systems have recently adopted vision-language models to match user dialogue intents with multimodal product information. However, extending these methods to many product domains faces a dilemma: deploying a separately adapted VLM per domain scales cost linearly with the number of domains and requires routing each dialogue to the right model, while naively merging all domains into a single VLM degrades accuracy because product characteristics vary widely across categories. LightCRS precomputes multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. articles.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) struggle with classical planning, but benchmarks rarely distinguish structural difficulty from the difficulty of interpreting symbolic vocabulary. We examine seven STRIPS domains with BFS-optimal plan lengths. For predicting structural difficulty without solving an instance, the zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic $h_{\mathrm{add}}$ outperforms learned alternatives on held-out domains (mean Spearman $|\rho|=0.931$), including ridge regression ($0.707$), object count ($0.657$), and the episodic retrieval architecture ARC ($0.400$). ARC also fails to outperform a linear model using the same features. To isolate semantic effects, we progressively rename predicates while preserving states, transitions, and optimal plans. articles.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on reusable skills. However, scaling skill libraries makes efficient and accurate skill use difficult. Full skill loading incurs high token and runtime overhead. In contrast, flat semantic retrieval treats skills as independent text entries, ignoring dependencies, execution order, state transitions, and data flow constraints. We propose SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework for efficient skill use in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions derived from successful executions. For a new task, SPEM reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates when available. Otherwise, it retrieves atomic skills and invokes Skill-GNN for state- and structure-aware skill selection. articles.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. articles.title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27028v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A poker agent can make a legal move and still make a strategically poor one. We ask whether compact AI agents can exhibit strategic behavior under hidden information and whether preference optimization can improve beyond static and zero-shot policies. We first evaluate a static baseline and three frozen language models: SmallThinker, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 whose performance varies substantially between exact-game and six-player evaluation. We therefore propose Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE), combining teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, and compare it with SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27045v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. It develops the foundations of physical AI across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems begin to resolve open research problems, reliable verification becomes increasingly important. Formal mathematics provides a trusted framework for mathematical reasoning, enabling agents to produce machine-checkable proofs while conducting mathematical exploration. Existing formal mathematics benchmarks often focus on known results or a small set of prominent open problems, which can become difficult to evaluate reliably once solutions are discovered and widely disseminated. Existing evaluation protocols are also not always aligned with how modern coding agents operate. We therefore introduce ReuF2F, a Lean 4 benchmark of 244 formalized open problems drawn from Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), spanning entry-level open research problems across a broad range of mathematical subfields. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27099v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical care, health-system operations and biomedical discovery depend on extracting reliable answers from patient records, yet applying diverse clinical questions across entire populations remains computationally expensive. Here we present Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter decision model for fast, typed judgments from clinical records, along with two agentic harnesses in which CS1 works together with a generalist language model. CS1-4B is trained on 12.4 million questions and answers from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system, combining structured-data keys, observed outcomes and language-model supervision across clinical notes, diagnostic reports and patient timelines. It answers multiple typed questions in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, and each answer carries a probability that can route uncertain cases to human review. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents act on the external world through tools and third-party skills, so a single executed action can cause irreversible harm. Existing defenses judge a proposed action without tracking whether its content comes from the user or from external sources such as tool outputs, and they judge it in isolation rather than against an available alternative, which forces a trade-off between security and utility. We present PROVISO, a controller that decides which action to commit after the agent proposes an action and before it is executed. PROVISO encodes trusted observations, external observations, the proposed action, and an alternative into provenance-typed memory, relates them through role-specific queries, and commits the action with the highest calibrated value learned from outcomes. articles.title: PORA: Learning When More Reasoning Pays Off for LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27119v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents perform tasks over multiple steps and revise their actions based on feedback. As the total reasoning budget is often limited and must support future steps, the agent must choose between short and long reasoning before each action. Longer reasoning may improve the final task outcome by preventing later errors, but it also uses budget capacity that may be needed for future decisions. This creates two challenges: estimating the downstream value of long reasoning and deciding when that value is worth using the remaining budget. We propose Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), which learns this decision by comparing short and long reasoning from the same interaction state. During training, \method{} completes the task twice from each selected state, once with a short reasoning allowance and once with a long allowance, and compares their final quality and total processing to estimate when longer reasoning is valuable. Abstract: Disaggregated \textsc{LLM} serving separates prefill and decode across node pools, placing a network fabric between \textsc{KV}-cache computation and consumption. Abstract: When training LLMs to code with reinforcement learning, reward hacking is often detectable but difficult to prevent, since (a) environment hardening is increasingly difficult as training environments grow more complex; and (b) training-time interventions incentivize models to obfuscate hacking behavior to bypass detection.
  We instead study whether we can predict when detectable reward hacking becomes dominant before executing an RL run, enabling us to select lower-risk recipes in advance. We find that the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset, which varies substantially across training recipes and repeated runs. Abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. For reward modeling, EM-EDM clusters demonstrations by latent reward functions and induces cluster-specific policies, and THEMES partitions trajectories into temporally coherent sub-trajectories guided by a hierarchically learned reward regulator; across one educational and three clinical datasets, THEMES outperforms flat and hierarchical AL baselines. articles.content:

Abstract: RLVR improves language-model reasoning, but commonly relies on independent stochastic rollouts for exploration, which can repeatedly sample similar failed strategies. Prior work has seen success with approaches that guide exploration by introducing dependence into the sampling process by including incorrect solutions in the context for subsequent attempts. Still, these methods introduce the additional question of how to assign credit to each attempt. We propose to view the credit assignment through the lens of Stochastic Shortest Paths, a framework in classical reinforcement learning that seeks to minimize the expected cumulative cost to reach a terminal state (in our case, a verified successful response). We show that, under suitable simplifying assumptions, this perspective naturally leads to a simple modification to GRPO, which we call Retry-Aware Policy Optimization (ReAPO). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28771v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Objects move, cameras pan, and weather drifts with the wind: much of what changes in sequential data is motion. Motion changes where things are, not what they are, and is therefore a symmetry of the data. Yet standard recurrent networks are not equivariant to it: their memory stays put while the input moves on. Flow equivariant recurrent networks first brought this symmetry into sequence models, for motions of constant velocity, or flows, by enumerating a bank of velocities. We extend this idea in three directions: from simple recurrent networks to convolutional LSTMs, from flows to motions whose velocity changes in time, and from enumerating velocities to estimating them. Treating a sequence as a field over time, we show that motion becomes a gauge symmetry: a global symmetry made local in time. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28773v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Non-uniform allocation can improve post-training pruning of large language models, yet quality can still degrade sharply at high sparsity. To control degradation as sparsity increases, we introduce LADDER (Layer-Wise Allocation via Damage-Driven Evaluation and Refinement), which allocates sparsity incrementally. At each step, it evaluates pruning an additional fraction of weights from each eligible layer and commits the layer update that causes the least end-to-end degradation per removed parameter. This process produces non-uniform sparsity profiles and exactly nested masks across multiple budgets. We evaluate LADDER on five OPT, Llama, and Qwen models across 10-90% sparsity, using SparseGPT as its candidate-generation backend and comparing against uniform and adaptive allocation baselines. articles.title: Second Thoughts: Exploring and Planning through Comparative Imagination in World Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28779v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World models let agents compare imagined outcomes before acting, but an agent must still decide which alternatives to explore and when a proposed plan should replace its learned policy. We introduce SDI (Sibling Disagreement in Imagination), which connects these decisions through a shared actor-based reference. SDI compares action sequences imagined from the same model state, using repeated rollouts of the actor's own sequence to measure variation under fixed behavior. This reference scales both the spread across candidate returns, which provides an exploration signal, and a proposed plan's predicted advantage, which governs action acceptance. The agent executes a planned action when its advantage exceeds the reference variability by a fixed factor; otherwise, it follows the actor. Unlike traditional and even recent LLM-augmented approaches that ultimately rely on clustering vector embeddings, our framework leverages LLM capabilities directly for the entire pipeline. Abstract: Iterative ML agents develop models by editing code, running experiments, reading a validation score, and choosing what to try next. In this work, we introduce an explicit feedback contract for ML-agent harnesses, which specifies what an agent may observe, when iteration should stop, and when the test split may be touched. The contract releases a validation score only when a submission clears a noise threshold computed from the paired standard error, so no margin has to be tuned. We ran experiments on click-through-rate prediction, learning to rank, and a control task with no signal to find. Abstract: While statistical learning has made remarkable progress in recent decades, driven by large datasets and data-driven protocols that have transformed scientific practice, it still faces a key limitation: it struggles to generalize beyond the data it has seen, often failing under distribution shift. Causality offers a promising solution: causal models focus on the underlying mechanisms of change rather than surface-level associations, enabling robust reasoning under external interventions. This allows systems not only to learn from data, but also to reason about hypothetical scenarios, adapt to new environments, and inform better decisions. articles.title: A Mechanistic Study of Automated Failure Attribution in LLM-based Agentic Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28811v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic systems have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks by enabling multiple interacting large language model (LLM)-based agents to collaborate and execute subtasks in parallel. However, this collaborative structure introduces new challenges for reliably evaluating and diagnosing system failures, particularly failure attribution: tracing a system's execution to identify the agent step responsible for an incorrect final outcome. Because manually performing this task is time- and labor-intensive, recent work has turned to LLMs as judges to automate the process, referred to as automated failure attribution (AFA). These approaches assume that a sufficiently capable model can infer the failing step directly from an interaction transcript. articles.title: When Do Gaussian Priors Fail? A Latent Geometry Investigation of RL Fine-Tuning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28849v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Latent diffusion models almost universally place a Gaussian prior on the VAE latent space. For base generation this default is unproblematic; under reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, however, it carries a structural limitation. The standard VAE's KL term does not merely ignore mode structure - it actively taxes separation and tightness. When data are multimodal, the ELBO optimum compresses distinct modes into an overlapping latent. RL fine-tuning amplifies this overlap: the score network is under-resolved on the saddle region between modes, dynamic-to-variational amplification rises sharply, and the collapse boundary beta_c is pushed far above its variational scale. On the real alanine-dipeptide Boltzmann distribution, a Gaussian-prior VAE collapses at beta_c = 0.224 while a mode-tracked Gaussian-mixture prior collapses at 0.00316, a 71x gap from the same pipeline.

A frozen system trains only a 22.6M-parameter CTC reader over a mix of encoder layers; an adapted system adds 3.1M low-rank adapter parameters, a 41.5M-parameter hybrid CTC/attention reader and joint decoding with a sub-word language model. articles.title: Translation and data ethics
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28710v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This chapter introduces data ethics for translation and discusses a number of ethical issues regarding data. These include issues of copyright, ownership and bias, which apply to all types of data, whereas there are further issues particular to minoritised language communities and those on either side of the digital divide, as data is implicated in power imbalances and dynamics. We close with a discussion of responsibility and regulation, and reflect on the growing attention on data ethics from translation studies researchers.

articles.title: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28767v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current evaluation of LLMs on benchmarks typically aggregates performance over individual examples into a single scalar score. This approach is overly coarse and ignores the diverse scope of skills covered by benchmark datasets. To address this limitation and better exploit benchmark data, we propose SkillEval, a new evaluation framework that performs cross-model, skill-level analysis. The framework integrates advances from two areas: (1) it leverages the meta-cognitive capabilities of LLMs to automatically discover interpretable skills from questions, and (2) it applies cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) from psychometrics to estimate per-skill abilities of LLMs. We conduct experiments on 3,811 LLMs evaluated on 9,523 items across five benchmarks spanning diverse domains (MATH, BBH, GPQA, MuSR, IFEval). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28772v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Psychotherapy fidelity assessment measures how faithfully a therapist adheres to a treatment protocol, a critical determinant of positive patient outcomes. However, fidelity assessment is bottlenecked by manual expert review, rendering the process labor-intensive and unscalable. To scale therapy supervision and support clinician self-learning, we present an integrated application of large language models (LLMs) that automates psychotherapy fidelity workflows and generates actionable supervisory feedback from authentic, long-form clinical transcripts. We evaluate three open-weight models across multiple task decomposition configurations and reasoning strategies, demonstrating that evidence-first reasoning improves fidelity estimation. articles.title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28787v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28799v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In case-based legal reasoning, legal professionals identify legally significant fact patterns in a new dispute and compare them with those of decided cases. In AI & Law, HYPO dimensions and CATO factors represent these patterns symbolically, organizing expert knowledge distilled from case narratives as explicit, structured, interpretable, and auditable legal concepts and relations that support case comparison, legal argument, and precedent-based reasoning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for legal tasks, yet their internal organization of legal knowledge remains difficult to trace. We investigate whether LLMs form internal representations corresponding to all 26 CATO factors. Two research questions examine linear decodability and sparse localization with sparse autoencoders. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28819v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Common instruction following (IF) benchmarks, such as IFEval, evaluate the ability of language models (LMs) to follow simple constraints that can easily be verified programmatically. These same constraints, in turn, are used as reward signals for reinforcement learning. This design may lead to reward hacking of constraints, pushing models away from the main task. Recent attempts to address this resulted in benchmarks with richer constraints, but required expert labor, remained closed-access, and cannot be easily extended. We present Lift-Bench, an IF benchmark that asks a model to draft a document given a topic and a structured outline. Constraints are scoped to certain document sections, providing finer control over constraint density. Lift-Bench includes both verifiable and judged constraints, as well as a training counterpart, Lift-Train. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28823v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dependency parsing resource development for Arabic has largely focused on Modern Standard Arabic, leaving dialectal Arabic comparatively under-resourced. We introduce MADARTB, the first large-scale parallel dependency treebank spanning five city dialects: Beirut, Cairo, Doha, Rabat and Tunis, and extending an existing parallel MSA version. In total MADARTB consists of 5,000 sentences annotated using the CATiB dependency scheme. We analyze syntactic similarity across all city dialects and MSA. Although global construction profiles exhibit high similarity across varieties, local syntactic structures frequently diverge, revealing substantial structural variation across dialects. We further establish a cross-dialect dependency parsing comparison using a supervised parser and four LLMs. The supervised parser achieves 87.5% LAS, while the best LLM setup trails at 85.7% LAS across all six varieties on the test set. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28838v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-quality human-translated parallel corpora can improve cross-lingual transfer, but are typically too small for large-scale pretraining. Machine-translated web corpora help overcome this limitation, making parallel data available at pretraining scale. Standard multilingual pretraining, however, samples source documents and their translations independently, without explicitly using their parallel structure. We investigate how to use the parallel structure of the data to improve multilingual pretraining by concatenating each document with its translation in the same training sequence. We compare this parallel pretraining (PPT) approach with standard pretraining (SPT), training models from scratch at matched token budgets. Surprisingly, despite the benefits of parallel data reported in prior cross-lingual work, PPT alone does not consistently improve language understanding over SPT. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28840v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Early-grade reading screening is critical for identifying children at risk of reading difficulty. Existing AI-based screeners are often limited in the scope of their analyses and evaluation metrics, or are proprietary systems that lack transparent model specifications and evaluation. We present KIRA, a dual-pathway screening system that pairs word-level fluency scoring with detailed phoneme-level error detection. We adapt pretrained word and phoneme recognizers to children's speech, reducing word error rate from 13.88% to 8.84% and phoneme error rate from 41.66% to 23.00%. Powered by these child-adapted models, we implement Word Reading (WRE) and Oral Reading Fluency (ORF), two foundational tasks in K-2 screening. The system integrates these recognizers with a web-based teacher-facing interface presenting fluency scores alongside phoneme feedback for potential targeted intervention. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28886v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM judges increasingly mediate benchmark evaluation, model selection, data curation, and training. Their decisions are useful only when each judge responds reliably to changes affecting its scoring criterion. Existing methods for reliability testing perturb inputs with known expected effects on judge scores. Prominent LLM-judge testing harnesses combine human-authored perturbation recipes with synthetic test generation, leaving scorer-specific recipe ideation outside the automated pipeline. This limits their use to fixed perturbations and pre-assumed scorer types. We introduce SANE, an agent-based framework that encodes behavioral requirements for stochastic evaluators as reusable agent instructions. Given a scorer specification, implementation, and representative inputs, the pipeline first identifies scorer-specific capabilities, then automatically derives perturbation recipes and expected score relations for each. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28887v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. However, realizing this design requires more than diverse backgrounds. When experiments are costly, a team can test only a limited number of ideas, thereby creating the need to balance exploration and exploitation when selecting a subset of researchers to propose and execute new experiments. Furthermore, each result should shape what the team tries next. We therefore ask how AI researchers with different scientific backgrounds can build on one another's findings and sustain progress under a limited experimental budget. Abstract: Cross-tokenizer logits distillation enables knowledge transfer across model families, allowing students to learn from stronger or more specialized teachers. However, differences in vocabulary and segmentation make teacher and student next-token distributions difficult to align. Existing logits-based methods are easy to integrate into standard distillation pipelines, but often rely on restrictive heuristics or tokenizer-pair-specific choices. They may restrict supervision to shared vocabulary subsets, require manually selecting different objectives for different tokenizer pairs, or match only the observed chunk and its complement rather than individual alternative continuations. Abstract: Refusal directions have been shown to transfer cross-lingually with near-perfect effectiveness across safety-aligned languages (Wang et al., 2025), reportedly regardless of resource level. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28944v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Semantic leakage occurs when a concept in the prompt steers model generation about an entity, even though the concept is irrelevant to it (e.g., a person who likes yellow is said to work as a school bus driver). It has mostly been studied in settings where the concept is directly attributed to the entity the model is asked about. This leaves open whether leakage is a flawed heuristic, where the model builds a profile of that entity, or a much broader associative tendency, e.g., working across seemingly unrelated entities. We argue for the latter: even after removing the attribution of the concept to the specific entity, leakage persists. Next, we extend this idea to gender bias. Abstract: Scanning every passage in a long document seems thorough, but does it preserve more useful evidence or produce better answers? We compare 11 retrieval configurations spanning lexical and dense search, hybrid reranking, and full-document scanning with Jev, OpenAI Decisions, and Cloudflare Clef. Our evaluation uses 396 QASPER questions and 80 questions from eight complete textbooks, with common passages, a five-passage limit, and a fixed answer generator. Distillation and the gate add large gains on external responses, but after greedy regeneration, distillation adds a smaller gain and the gate little or none. Abstract: In vision and scientific domains involving spatial data, a key question is whether node feature values vary independently across space or form coherent spatial structures. Classical spatial autocorrelation statistics such as Moran's $I$ and Geary's $C$ quantify this phenomenon but operate on a single scalar variable with fixed neighbourhood weights, limiting their use for high-dimensional graph-like data. articles.title: Register Anything Model for Generalizable and Robust Point Cloud Registration
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28821v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Register Anything Model (RAM), a unified model for generalizable 3D point cloud registration that robustly estimates 6-DoF transformations across diverse domains spanning sensors and environments. Existing registration methods are typically tailored to a single domain, with carefully tuned architectures and hyperparameters, and thus degrade markedly when applied to novel domains. We bridge this gap by training a single model on diverse data from indoor, outdoor, and object domains. A central challenge is the severe geometric discrepancy across domains, i.e., differences in scene scale, sensor noise, point density, and structural patterns, which hinders processing with a unified point-based model. Abstract: Instruction-guided video generative models offer a scalable solution for stress-testing autonomous driving systems by simulating diverse environmental conditions. However, driving scenes operate within a dense Operational Design Domain (ODD) governed by strict traffic semantics. When applied to global driving-condition edits, general-purpose instruction-guided video editors frequently corrupt these semantics, leading to structural hallucinations and ``temporal shock.'' This work distills and protects traffic semantics during video editing at three levels. First, we construct a hybrid dataset by combining temporally aligned real-world videos with synthetic edits, balancing foundational scene structure with unambiguous appearance signals. Second, during training, we adapt advantage conditioning from offline reinforcement learning to align the model using dense rewards. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28835v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conventional visual sensing faces a fundamental dilemma: information that should remain private today may need to be recovered tomorrow. This challenge is becoming increasingly important as cameras become pervasive in our daily surroundings. Existing safeguards either protect visual content only after an image is formed or suppress information during capture in ways that prevent its later recovery. Here, we show through an information-theoretic analysis that privacy and recoverability cannot be achieved simultaneously in static optical systems. Information preserved in a measurement for later reconstruction also remains available to an observer of that measurement, limiting the privacy such systems can provide. Abstract: Few-shot image classification (FSIC) frequently suffers from visual ambiguity, where background clutter and RGB appearance similarities hinder discriminative feature matching in data-scarce settings. To mitigate this, we propose DAFIC, a geometry-guided framework that incorporates monocular depth into representation learning, episodic adaptation, and dense support-query matching. DAFIC first learns geometry-aware token representations through RGB-D self-supervised pre-training. Subsequently, the Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation (DGA) module uses depth-derived geometry to refine patch representations with geometry-enriched class context while suppressing background interference. Spatial Bidirectional Patch Matching (SBiM) then performs bidirectional dense matching on the refined features, reducing sensitivity to spurious correspondences and background clutter. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28858v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distilled diffusion models generate high-quality images in a few sampling steps, but aligning them with task requirements and human preferences is difficult. Methods developed for multi-step diffusion models rely on differentiable rewards, or on score fields and stochastic trajectories that distilled generators may lack. We ask whether a few-step generator can be adapted using only external reward evaluations and reference samples, and show that two binary classifiers suffice. Our method, DualHeads, implements them as lightweight heads on a frozen diffusion backbone. The reward head learns which samples of the same prompt score higher, the reference head separates reference images from generated ones, and the generator maximizes a weighted sum of their logits. Abstract: Selecting intermediate features from a frozen diffusion model for discriminative tasks is non-trivial because the useful signal is distributed across the denoising trajectory, network depth, and channels. In practice, this requires choosing a timestep, a block, and a channel subset. Existing methods either fix these choices by hand or optimize only a few extraction hyperparameters, most often the timestep, then reuse the same rule across inputs and budgets. We introduce Policy-Mask, a budget-conditioned policy trained on the downstream objective that jointly selects all three under a prescribed channel budget. Without normalization, the channel-score contribution grows with the number of selected channels and dominates the timestep and block updates. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28899v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesised data is a common strategy to address the lack of annotated handwritten music scores in Optical Music Recognition (OMR). Smashcima is a recent synthesis framework that assembles pages of handwritten scores by sampling glyph images from MUSCIMA++ and positioning them with hard-coded rules. In this work we ask whether these rules are grounded empirically and whether a learned model for context-dependent positioning can further improve synthesis quality. We extract inter-glyph distributions from around 285 thousand annotated relationships across MUSCIMA++ and OmniOMR, finding that several key parameters deviate systematically from real handwriting. Replacing these constants with empirical means reduces positioning RMSE by up to 60%. articles.title: MINER: Modeling Inter- and Intra-Person Variance for Reidentification
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification (CC-ReID) remains challenging due to drastic appearance shifts across outfits. Most prior works devise biometric signal-extraction heuristics to enhance inter-person variance, e.g., using segmentation masks, while leaving intra-person variance uncontrolled. We present MINER, a simple model-agnostic framework that suppresses garment bias by contrasting hard examples and adaptively balancing dataset-dependent intra- and inter-person variance. Extensive experiments show that MINER improves retrieval across CC-ReID benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on four datasets and ranking among the leaders in all three tracks of the open TVRID RGB-Depth ReID challenge.

Abstract: Coarse-to-real (C2R) video generation converts coarse animation, simulation, or game-rendered videos into photorealistic videos while preserving scene layout, camera motion, and dynamics. Training such models requires aligned (coarse, realistic) video pairs, which are expensive to create and confine prior systems to narrow synthetic domains. We exploit a simple asymmetry: paired videos are hard to obtain, but paired real-to-coarse images are easy to construct with existing editing and 3D reconstruction tools. Using these image pairs, we train the DINO-R2C model to transfer realistic images to coarse images in DINO feature space, and apply it frame-wise to ordinary real videos to synthesize pseudo-coarse videos. The C2R# model then learns to generate each real video from its pseudo-coarse counterpart, free from needing (coarse, realistic) video pairs. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate 6-DoF object pose tracking is essential for robotic interaction, yet conventional monocular pipelines frequently suffer from catastrophic divergence under rapid object motion. We present RoPT, a robust tracking framework engineered to overcome this limitation by unifying visual perception, temporal kinematics, and global re-localization into a tightly coupled closed loop. Unlike existing open-loop trackers, RoPT delivers three critical capabilities that fundamentally alter system resilience. First, the visual perception component tracks object masks to robustly handle partial and severe occlusions. Second, a kinematic factor graph regularizes frame-to-frame updates, forecasts forward pose predictions, and drives a parallel multi-hypothesis verification scheme to bypass local minima. Abstract: The scarcity of large annotated datasets limits deep learning (DL) segmentation in material CT analysis. DL-based pseudo-labeling can help, but it is often computationally expensive and hard to interpret. We introduce a multi-stage, model-free framework that generates pseudo-labels directly from grayscale CT scans. It combines thresholding, morphological dilation, and a custom breadth-first search region-growing algorithm to produce polygonal annotations without pre-trained weights, labeled data, or a GPU. We compare it against the zero-shot Segment Anything Model (SAM), a fully supervised 3D U-Net, and classical baselines. Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) platforms typically return several images per prompt so users can explore different visual interpretations and choose one that matches their intent. However, T2I models are usually optimized for single-image quality which comes at a cost of multi-image diversity, limiting this exploration. Diversity is also contextual: one user wants variations in background, while another wants them in artistic style, and the same user may later want variations in clothing. Abstract: In recent years, automated fruit classification systems have become a more critical component in precision agriculture for efficient yield estimation, quality control, and supply chain optimization. However, they still face significant challenges under varying quality, fruit maturity, illumination, texture degradation, morphological attributes, domain shift, and post-harvest handling conditions. This is a real-world setting where models that have been trained on specific quality grades must generalize to unseen grades to handle significant domain shift. articles.title: Real-Time Ground Normal Vector Estimation for Spherical Mobile 3D Mapping using LiDAR-Inertial Odometry
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28701v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate ground plane normal estimation is essential for odometry in spherical mobile mapping systems (SMMS), which face challenges from rapid rotations and limited ground coverage. We propose two RANSAC-based approaches: single-scan estimation with normal vector scoring and multi-step validation, and LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO)-based estimation using a global 3D map. Evaluated across diverse real-world datasets against terrestrial laser scanner ground truth, results show that LIO-based estimation significantly outperforms single-scan methods in accuracy and robustness. Integrating ground normal estimates into the motion model improves pose estimation, supporting autonomous navigation in challenging and hazardous environments.

Abstract: In human-robot interaction (HRI) tasks, humans may interact with the robot in either an active guiding or passive following state, resulting in distinct control objectives for each interaction mode. Most existing approaches rely on predefined switching thresholds to distinguish interaction modes, but their performance can be sensitive to measurement noise. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. First, a neural network (NN) trained via meta-learning is developed to recognize human intention without manually defined thresholds. By successfully incorporating force-dependent parameters from the controller, the recognition rates are improved from 90.1\% to 99.1\% for the passive mode and from 79.8\% to 97.1\% for the active mode. Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating a robust wrench observer with a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). Abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Abstract: Long-horizon robotic operation requires memory that scales with essential information rather than execution time. We present a parameter-space memory framework where each episode is stored as a separable object. Crucially, this delta remains a fixed size regardless of whether the episode spans a hundred or a hundred thousand frames. On RoboMME, the language model exceeds chance across all question types, and the decoder achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.51. Abstract: Trajectory demonstrations show robots how to behave but not why, leaving them to guess which features of the task actually matter. Incorrect guesses produce misaligned internal representations and lead to incorrect robot behaviors. Because task features are often semantically defined, we argue that natural language is better suited for specifying features rather than relying on demonstrations. articles.title: Learning Dynamic Games for Cooperative Iterative Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider cooperative and iterative tasks involving multiple agents whose interactions are modeled as a dynamic game with shared constraints. We propose a general learning framework applicable to nonlinear and nonconvex dynamic games that uses previously executed feasible trajectories to construct a sampled joint safe set and player-specific cost-to-go functions. At each time step, the agents jointly select a previously sampled terminal state and a Generalized Nash equilibrium used to reach it. A new solution is adopted only if it satisfies a cooperative acceptance rule agreed upon by the players. The framework accommodates individual non-degradation requirements and selection criteria such as weighted costs and Nash bargaining. We show that the proposed framework guarantees recursive feasibility and characterize conditions under which each player's cost is non-increasing across iterations.

Abstract: Blind and visually impaired individuals face uncertainty when navigating unfamiliar areas. Whether a cane or a guide dog is used for navigation, this may prove to be challenging. To mitigate this challenge, we present the Context-Aware Navigation Explanation framework that explains guide dog movements for obstacle avoidance and navigation using a large language model. This system integrates perceptual context with planned future trajectories to generate natural-language explanations of robot movement. We deploy the system on a Unitree Go2 platform in indoor navigation scenarios and evaluate how different explanation context configurations affect user trust and explanation satisfaction. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern robotic agents are increasingly expected to support steerable control, where a single policy can adjust its behavioral style at runtime under changing user preferences. Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning provides this interface, but conditioning alone does not ensure that a requested behavior change is strong, does not leak into unrelated behaviors, and does not compromise task performance. Our evaluation combines Preference Reward Responsiveness (PRR) with coverage and utility metrics. articles.content:

Abstract: Mobile manipulators must adapt not only to objects, but also to the spatial context in which they appear: where to position the base, how to manipulate, and where to look while navigating surrounding scene geometry. On whole-body dexterous grasping, COWBOY transfers zero-shot to hundreds of objects and diverse in-the-wild scenes, spanning cluttered tabletops, shelves, drawers, and other unstructured settings. articles.title: GGraph: A GPU-Accelerated Library for Graph-Based Robot Deployment and Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28953v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous mobile robots require spatial representations that capture geometry and semantics while staying sparse enough for planning in large, unknown environments. Graphs provide a natural representation for this purpose and underpin both classical planning methods and a growing class of reinforcement-learning (RL) policies. However, RL training needs hundreds to thousands of parallel environments, each constructing and updating its own graph. Existing graph libraries are typically designed for either single-robot deployment or fixed graphs, and CPU-based graph construction limits scalable training to only a few dozen environments. We introduce GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library for both robot deployment and large-scale learning. Abstract: Safe robotic task planning requires planners that can reliably achieve task goals while satisfying safety constraints. Classical planners search over explicit symbolic task representations and can provide formal guarantees with respect to encoded safety constraints, but require rigid input formats. Thus, they can be difficult to deploy locally on robotic systems with limited resources. Abstract: Vision-based insertion requires correcting alignment errors while retaining useful behavior learned from demonstrations. Abstract: Human-in-the-loop (HIL) post-training improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies through expert corrections, but costly human supervision and repeated real-robot evaluation limit algorithm exploration and development. articles.title: 具身记忆赛道持续升温，长记忆迎来新 SOTA
articles.content: IROS 2026 最佳论文启示录：没有长记忆的机器人，终将被淘汰。    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       本月初在匹兹堡闭幕的 IROS 2026 将最佳论文奖颁给了 LT-Mem，这项研究让机器人重访同一空间时，能完整保留每个物体的位置变迁史，而非仅仅记住最新一次看到的样子。评委会从近两千篇收录论文中选中它，想必不仅是认可其扎实的工作，也是代表学界宣告：具身长记忆（long-term embodied memory）已经从一个工程补丁，变成了机器人领域公认的科学问题。从实际角度考虑，通用机器人要规模化落地，需要以小时、天乃至周为单位持续运行，而不只是几分钟。没有长记忆，每次相遇都是初次见面，机器人只是一个个孤立的单次动作执行器；有了长记忆，它才能从一次性工具变成可以长期上岗的同事。但解决这件事远不是扩大上下文窗口那么简单：持续涌入的多模态数据既无法全部存储，也无法全部检索；现实世界还在不断变化，新的观察既不能简单覆盖旧的，也不能无序堆叠；更棘手的是，一条错误的记忆会在之后的决策里被反复调用，错误由此层层放大。记忆如何写入、如何留证、如何纠错，都是需要被正面回答的问题，靠调几个工程参数解决不了。AI科技评论（雷峰网公众号）注意到，在这一方向被顶会加冕的数月前，国内具身初创公司贝塔无限就已坐上牌桌。今年五月，贝塔的联合创始人陶帅在采访中明确表示：长效、多模态、时空记忆的缺失，是他们首先要重点突破的方向。随后，团队陆续发布 BetaMem 全时空多模态记忆架构、世界动作模型 BetaWAM 0.1、首款机器人多米。10 月 20 日，团队把 BetaMem 的写入学习、证据管理和自我改进机制写成了系统的方法与实验，挂上 arXiv。论文交出的成绩单颇为亮眼：BetaMem 采用 9B 开源模型生成记忆，在 M3-Bench-robot、LoCoMo、OpenEQA 和 EgoLifeQA 四项代表性记忆基准的对比评测中均取得 SOTA 成绩。尤其在串联多次观察中的线索、回忆长时间跨度的事件、识别个人习惯等任务上，BetaMem 展现出明显优势——这些能力，正是机器人进入生活、持续积累对人与环境的了解所需要的。LT-Mem 从多会话建图切入，把问题收窄到干净、可评测；BetaMem 则从记忆如何形成、如何验证、如何从失败中学习的系统视角，搭建完整的记忆底座。一边是顶尖学术单点攻坚摘得顶会桂冠，一边是国内团队以产业落地为目标搭建完整记忆底座，学术和产业在此交汇，足以证明长记忆是整个领域正在收敛的核心方向判断。01记忆这道题，学界做到哪一步围绕机器人长期记忆，学界探索了许多方法。按年份罗列意义不大，AI科技评论（雷峰网公众号）想换个角度，看记忆回答了什么问题，还剩什么没回答。第一类关注空间侧的记忆，也就是“这里有什么”。Hydra、ConceptGraphs 等三维场景图把物体、地点、房间组织成可被语言查询的关系网，Khronos 把时间引入动态环境建图，DynaMem 让移动操作机器人在物体被挪动后继续更新记忆，真机上对非静止物体的取放成功率平均达 70%，是静态系统的两倍以上。这一支空间关系清楚，但记住的主要是当下这一版世界长什么样。第二类关注检测类的记忆，也就是“我见过什么”。ReMEmbR 把长时导航视频建成可检索的时空记忆，供智能体推理。但检索按相似度排序，取回的是过去的信息。五分钟前桌上确实有杯子，现在还在不在呢？检索不负责回答。第三类关注变化侧的记忆，也就是“它变了没有”。LT-Mem 正是这一思路。论文把现有系统的毛病命名为“时间性失忆”：要么用新观测覆盖旧状态，要么存下语义快照却没有跨次访问一致的物体身份。它用一个随物体习性变化的易变性分数，决定新观察该覆盖、保持还是并存。作者也坦承局限：测试只覆盖两个室内加一个室外场景、各 10 次访问，外观相似物体的身

The new class of shares, meanwhile, will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend. Holders will get one share of the new stock in what will essentially be a two-for-one stock split, Meta said. It expects trading of the new shares to begin in January. articles.title: Agentic World Action Models
articles.content: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.

articles.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose $\textbf{LongZero}$, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs.

articles.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
articles.content: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model should compress. We build CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions. Its members differ only in a small bottleneck on frozen features and share a diffusion decoder self-distilled to one or a few steps. We train the same world model on each autoencoder in two domains, manipulation and navigation, with two environments each. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera. Our study also leads to four findings. At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality. Code, models and a live demo are at https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre

articles.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
articles.content: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. These observations motivate a shift from fixed-depth computation to item-level adaptive reasoning. To this end, we propose LoopRec. LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block and introduces a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary that makes a binary exit-or-continue decision for every item independently. Items whose representations have sufficiently matured exit early, while those requiring deeper reasoning continue to subsequent recursions. This design converts the fixed global depth into a learned, per-item property without auxiliary depth labels, and is readily adaptable to diverse backbone architectures. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks with four backbone families demonstrate that LoopRec consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. Further analysis reveals that LoopRec's learned allocation exhibits interpretable patterns aligned with our post-hoc oracle analysis: lower-frequency items and more recent interactions naturally receive deeper computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec.

articles.title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
articles.content: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program can isolate task-relevant regions and boundaries directly from scene meshes, and a downstream pose program can measure the resulting geometry to compute a target $SE(3)$ pose. Visual and numerical feedback from execution lets the model inspect intermediate selections and candidate placements to iteratively revise its code. To evaluate open-ended placement across functional use, geometric fit, and contextual arrangements, we introduce the 71-task VoxProg-Bench benchmark along with an evaluation suite pairing perceptual Intent Alignment and 3D Physical Validity. Across VoxProg-Bench and external benchmarks, VoxProg consistently outperforms relation-based, keypoint-based, and mesh-based baselines.

articles.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
articles.content: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. Our method encodes an exploratory interaction clip collected within the test scene into a compact physics descriptor token, which grounds subsequent predictions in the scene's actual physical behavior. PhysiCalWorld is trained end-to-end with the latent prediction loss alone, without physics labels. At inference time, the descriptor token is extracted once and can be reused across rollouts with negligible compute overhead. We evaluate PhysiCalWorld across four environments covering diverse physics variations and show that it substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate. The learned descriptors also form a physically structured latent space and generalize beyond the physics ranges seen during training.

articles.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
articles.content: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection. However, existing encoders typically specialize in only one or two of these capabilities; we therefore introduce ALPS, a pretrained visual state encoder that unifies all three in a single set of patch tokens. Using only still images and text, we pretrain a ViT-B/16 from scratch with language, reconstruction, and spatial correspondence objectives, and then refine it via cross-view self-distillation. In a unified evaluation across fifteen public encoders, ALPS achieves the lowest aggregate LIBERO state-probe error among ViT-B models (matching the 3.5x larger V-JEPA 2-L) while maintaining strong language alignment and accurate pixel reconstruction. Downstream, frozen ALPS tokens reach the highest mean policy success on LIBERO (85.5%) when paired with our native text tower, match or exceed leading encoders on world-model planning across PushT, Wall, and Granular, and allow predicted future tokens to be decoded directly into pixels for visual inspection. We hope this work helps establish visual pretraining as a shared foundation for understanding, prediction, and action in world models.
